A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StaR-KVQA framework, with matching methods, experiments, figures and tables. All pages are readable. v2 ends with references; v3 adds Appendices A–E, which were included in the comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original StaR-KVQA experiments on OK-VQA and FVQA, including component ablations, candidate-count sensitivity and cross-domain transfer results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results and adds aggregate ablation scores in Table 3.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.5 retain the dual-path planner, path-conditioned composer, coverage filtering, same-model selector, training objective and single-pass inference. Appendix C introduces analytical assumptions, without documenting changes to the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation remain on OK-VQA and FVQA, including transfer in both directions and the same qualitative examples. No additional dataset, task or test scenario is evaluated.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain the same comparison methods, and Table 4 retains the Frozen and SFT comparators for each backbone. Appendix A expands descriptions of existing baselines without adding evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The reported backbones, training settings, candidate counts, answer normalization, direct-answer accuracy and transfer protocols remain unchanged. Appendices A–B expand existing protocol documentation; Table 3's averages summarize retained accuracy columns rather than changing the underlying evaluation.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 3, candidate-count sensitivity and timing in Figure 3, transfer analysis in Table 4, and cases in Tables 5–6 are retained. The added averages introduce no new ablation condition or analysis question.

E5.justification: Appendix A.1 newly specifies that seed 42 applies to data loading, parameter initialization and decoding. Both versions already report single-run results; v3 adds no repeated runs, confidence intervals or other uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds six averages across the existing backbone/dataset settings, including 86.27 for StaR-KVQA and 78.80 without the selector. The underlying scores in Tables 1–4, Figure 3's curves and the qualitative outputs remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix C introduces trace-feasibility definitions and assumptions, a Rademacher-complexity claim, an MLE/MAP interpretation of selection, a KL-based risk lemma and self-distillation theorem, and a likelihood lower-bound proposition with derivation. These substantial formal additions have no counterparts in v2.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims: structured trace supervision, a single-model pipeline without external retrieval, improved accuracy and transparency, and up to +11.3% improvement on OK-VQA.

C2.justification: The introduction adds deployment constraints and explicitly positions IK-KVQA as complementary to retrieval-based systems. Appendices B–C add metric-choice rationale and probabilistic interpretations of existing components. The empirical interpretations and limitations concerning hallucination and explanation faithfulness remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly identifies Dynamic Thinking mode for both Gemini variants and clarifies the use of default decoding temperature and generation length without model-specific tuning. Most software, hardware and training hyperparameters repeat information already provided in v2.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Word2Vec and two Wen–Fang papers on graph-augmented low-resource text classification. It also clarifies the complementary relationship to retrieval-based KVQA, while retaining the existing novelty and self-distillation positioning.

P1.justification: v3 revises the title and affiliations, rewrites deployment motivation, condenses the approach and contribution summaries, and merges the LLM/MLLM related-work discussion. It adds acknowledgements and appendices, while preserving the main section order and most method and experimental prose.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains an Average column, Figure 1's caption is shortened, and the author block and experimental displays are compacted or repositioned. Tables 5–6 now appear together on page 8. The existing diagrams, plots and case illustrations are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves scope clarification and implementation disclosure, but its new theoretical support introduces a rigor problem absent from v2. Appendix C.2's claimed complexity contraction does not follow from its assumptions: restricting traces need not restrict answer hypotheses. Appendix C.1 also assumes visual attestability not specified by Section 4.2. These weaknesses outweigh the modest reporting gains, while the unchanged method and empirical evidence limit the deterioration.
